language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, my name is Joao. I'm 8 years old and I'm from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil's most famous city and known for its parade called Carnival.
A few weeks ago I learned about how boiling water works. I also learned about the water cycle. Now I need to study for my next test, but I forgot some things. Can you help me refresh my memory?

I can tell you what I remember so far. When liquid boils it becomes gas. At a certain temperature the molecules will gain enough energy to break free and become gas. This is called the boiling point. The boiling point for water is 100 degree Celsius.
However, gas can become liquid again. How is this possible? The opposite of boiling is called condensation. It takes place when vapor in the air condenses from gas back into liquid form.
Do you know how the water cycle works?

Terrific!

Let's take a look at the water cycle. The water cycle has different stages and begins with rain falling from the sky. Eventually, the rainwater ends up in the rivers and oceans. The sun heats the water and the water evaporates. The evaporated water forms clouds. Then the water in the clouds cools and becomes liquid again. Once the clouds get too heavy, the water falls to the Earth again as rain.
Let's take a look at the cycle more closely. I'll tell you about a stage in the cycle. Do you think you can tell me what name that stage has?
